content: Russell's sign refers to the presence of scarring on the knuckles or the back of the hand, which results from repeated self-induced vomiting over an extended period. This scarring typically occurs when the affected individual makes contact with their incisor teeth while using their fingers to stimulate the gag reflex at the back of the throat. This type of scarring is considered a physical manifestation of an underlying mental health condition. Russell's sign is most commonly observed in individuals with eating disorders, such as bulimia nervosa or anorexia nervosa. However, it is important to note that the presence of Russell's sign is not always a definitive indicator of an eating disorder. In some cases, the scarring associated with Russell's sign can be treated dermatologically using urea-based treatments. Individuals with bulimia who are capable of hands-free purging — a method of inducing vomiting by voluntarily opening the esophageal sphincter (the lower throat flap) in a manner similar to belching, while contracting the stomach muscles — rarely exhibit Russell's sign. This is because hands-free purging does not involve the insertion of fingers into the throat, thereby avoiding trauma to the hands during the act of purging.
